key_takeaways: The gov.gr civil licence entry (updated 5 November 2026) lists eight days to complete: a seven-day wait for objections, then one day to grant the licence.
The seven days start only when the town hall accepts a complete application, including the published newspaper notice; an incomplete file is returned and the process starts again.

A 4 January 2019 Interior Ministry circular indicates that a foreign certificate confirming you are free to marry can stand in for the licence when it also names your partner, and Chania's list for couples living abroad requires the partner to be named, while Heraklion's asks for a home-country licence, so confirm with DFAT and your town hall whether your Australian CNI names your partner.

Since 1 September 2021, official Greek translations come from a translator on the Greek Foreign Ministry's Register of Certified Translators or from a Greek consulate; no Greek source we read mentions NAATI.

A marriage valid in Greece is generally recognised in Australia without registration, but an Australian-born spouse who wants a new passport in a married name needs a change of name certificate from their state or territory registry first.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a marriage licence in Greece?
faq.a: The gov.gr civil licence entry lists eight days: a seven-day objection period, then one day to grant. The week starts only once the town hall accepts a complete application. Couples living abroad may not need a Greek licence at all; ask your town hall.

faq.q: Do Australians need to live in Greece to get married there?
faq.a: No. Chania and Heraklion publish document lists for foreigners living abroad, based on a document from your own country; Chania requires it to name your partner. Athens publishes a route only for its residents and for Greek citizens registered there, so ask the town hall where you plan to marry.

faq.q: Is a marriage in Greece legally recognised in Australia?
faq.a: In most cases, yes, if it was valid in Greece and would have been valid under Australian law. You cannot register it in Australia; your Greek certificate is the proof.

faq.q: Can same-sex couples legally marry in Greece?
faq.a: Yes. Law 5089/2024 provides for civil marriage between people of the same sex, and Australian law no longer determines the right to marry by sex or gender. This applies to civil ceremonies; confirm the documents for your own passports with your town hall.

faq.q: How long can Australians stay in Greece without a visa?
faq.a: Greece is in the Schengen area, and Smartraveller's Greece travel advice says Australians can stay 90 days or less without a visa in some cases. Register under the EU Entry/Exit System (EES), the EU's digital border record, on arrival, and before you book, check the status of ETIAS, the EU's travel authorisation scheme.
